jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, Enterprise - Healthcare Life Sciences (HLS)
jobs.description:
About The Team

Across industries, OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering (AIE) team helps organizations turn frontier AI into safe, reliable production systems that deliver meaningful business outcomes. We work directly with customers’ engineering, product, security, and transformation teams to navigate complex architectures, data environments, governance requirements, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better OpenAI products and reusable patterns that help customers move faster.

About The Role

As an Enterprise AIE, you will serve as a technical partner to leading organizations within the Healthcare and Life Sciences segment (HLS), helping them turn ambitious AI use cases into durable production systems and adoption at scale. You will combine deep technical judgment with hands-on engineering to provide technical leadership on complex customer deployments. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions about model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. You will work across clinical, operational, administrative and research workflows, translating security, privacy and governance requirements into practical deployment decisions. Success is measured by durable production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful business impact. Your deployment experience will also directly influence how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role may be based in one of our offices in New York City or San Francisco, or it may be performed remotely. Office-based employees follow a hybrid work model with three days per week in the office. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In This Role, You Will

Work hands-on in code to design, build, evaluate, and deploy AI systems from prototype to reliable production and scaled adoption that solve important customer problems and deliver measurable business outcomes.
Partner with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and success criteria.
Make sound technical decisions across model selection, agent and tool design, retrieval, context design, data pipelines, evaluation, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.
Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers to resolution.
Partner closely with customers’ engineering teams and OpenAI’s Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and Go-to-Market teams to turn deployment experience into actionable product feedback.
Partner with customer security, privacy, clinical and business teams to design responsible AI deployments, including data handling, access controls, evaluation, human oversight and monitoring.
Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

Have personally designed, built, and shipped AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, taking them from prototype to production and making substantial contributions through coding, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.
Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working end to end across model APIs, agent and tool development, retrieval and data pipelines, evaluation, observability, integrations, and production operations. Experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.
Know how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, automated graders, production signals, and human judgment.
Have navigated enterprise production requirements, including integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.
Have experience delivering AI or software in healthcare, life sciences or similarly complex regulated enterprises, with measurable outcomes beyond a proof of concept and familiarity with sensitive data, legacy systems and interoperability.
Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
Communicate clearly and credibly with hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security and product teams, and executives.
Take end-to-end ownership, exercise strong technical judgment, and move effectively through ambiguity.
Healthcare or life sciences experience is strongly preferred; strong candidates from other regulated enterprise environments are also encouraged to apply.
Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility. Prior OpenAI product experience is not required.

Discover more at www.asteralabs.com.

As a Physical Design & CAD Engineer
, you will serve as a Technical Lead developing Astera Labs’ next-generation connectivity ASICs for cloud and AI infrastructure.

This role combines Physical Design CAD methodology development with hands-on place-and-route (PNR) implementation. You will develop and optimize automated design flows for advanced process nodes while contributing to block-level physical design, timing closure, and GDSII signoff.

You will collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to improve design efficiency, automation, and silicon implementation.

Develop and maintain Physical Design CAD flows and methodologies for advanced process nodes.
Build automation frameworks using Python and Tcl to support synthesis through signoff.
Perform hands-on Physical Design and PNR, including floorplanning, placement, CTS, routing, and timing closure.
Develop and optimize EDA tool flows for timing analysis, extraction, EM/IR, and physical verification.
Support block-level implementation from synthesis through GDSII signoff.
Improve design quality, automation, and flow efficiency.
Collaborate with design, verification, and engineering teams to support ASIC development and tapeout.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field; Master's degree preferred.
5+ years of experience in ASIC Physical Design, CAD methodology, or design automation.
Strong understanding of physical design implementation and RTL-to-GDSII methodologies.
Experience developing or maintaining Physical Design CAD flows.
Hands-on experience with PNR, timing closure, and physical design signoff.
Proficiency in Python and/or Tcl scripting.
Experience with Cadence and/or Synopsys physical design tools.
Experience with advanced semiconductor process nodes (7nm or below).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with 3nm or more advanced process technologies.
Experience building automated CAD flows from synthesis through signoff.
Familiarity with Cadence Innovus, Tempus, Genus, Synopsys ICC2, Fusion Compiler, and PrimeTime.
Experience with EM/IR analysis, DRC/LVS, ECO, and timing signoff methodologies.
Experience with block-level ownership through tapeout.
Experience developing scalable CAD methodologies and automation frameworks.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is $160,000–$200,000 USD. Your salary will be determined based on your experience and the pay of employees in similar positions.

jobs.description:
The Stowers Institute has an opening for a Bioinformatics Specialist to assist the Computational Biology core facility with biological data processing and analysis. The Bioinformatics Specialist will use computational tools to process, transform, visualize, and analyze datasets primarily derived from high-throughput sequencing experiments. We are seeking an intellectually curious and motivated individual who will thrive in a collaborative, biology-driven team environment.
This is primarily an on-site position, with some flexibility for occasionally working from home. We value in-person collaboration but also support work-life balance.

Key Responsibilities:

Use R and Python to analyze and visualize high-throughput next-generation sequencing (NGS) data, from raw reads through downstream interpretation
Create analysis reports to organize results and share them with collaborators
Follow group best practices to maintain reproducibility and organize results

Minimum requirements:

Masters degree in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, or a related computationally oriented discipline
Demonstrated experience in NGS data analysis, including quality control, alignment, and downstream interpretation.
Experience working in a Unix/Linux environment
Interest in exploring and using generative AI
Basic understanding of and interest in Biology

Preferred skills:

Experience with a range of NGS applications (e.g., (sc)RNA-seq, ATAC-seq)
Experience with Bioconductor packages and Shiny
Experience with Python
Experience with cluster computing (Especially slurm)

The ideal candidate will have strong problem-solving abilities, excellent communication and organization skills, good attention to detail, biological interest and curiosity, and the ability to manage multiple projects effectively.

jobs.description:
Description

Drive transformation for leading Healthcare & Life Sciences organizations while shaping the future of patient care, drug discovery, and clinical innovation through AWS cloud and AI solutions.

Partner with senior leaders at global HCLS enterprises to accelerate their cloud adoption journey, delivering measurable business outcomes and strategic value.

About The Role

Customer Solutions Managers (CSMs) at AWS are obsessed with accelerating customer cloud adoption and driving measurable value from cloud investments. As a CSM in Healthcare & Life Sciences, you'll partner with senior leaders and engineering teams at global organizations to strategize and manage their end-to-end cloud and AI transformation journeys.

We help Healthcare & Life Sciences organizations adopt advanced cloud and AI solutions while migrating existing workloads to the cloud. Together with customers, we shape and execute strategies to build mindshare and broaden the use of AWS offerings across their enterprises.

If you are excited about the prospect of using your cloud architecture experience to assist our most valuable customers, tackling challenging problems, have a hand in shaping the future of cloud adoption, enhancing and growing your own skills, and having fun, then we would love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

You will be a critical partner to our customers, leveraging your experience with large scale cloud transformations and helping shepherd them through their stages of AWS adoption. Guiding the customer through the operational, educational, and governance aspects of a successful AWS cloud journey.

You will interface with customer and AWS leadership, driving collaboration between the other core account groups (Sales, Support, Solutions Architecture, and Professional Services), product/engineering teams, and customer teams, planning and supporting major workload migrations. You will translate strategic initiatives in the account plan into executable actions, working backwards from our customers key milestones. You will manage cadence by leading the reporting and tracking functions along the way. The execution of education plans, roadmap to business outcome alignments, Executive Briefing Sessions, and go-live events and transitions are a few items owned by the CSM that are critical to the success of our customer’s cloud journey.

You are encouraged to think big, invent and take ownership on customer challenges. You will not only bring the best of AWS/Amazon to our customers, you will proactively help solve the customer’s challenges through new ideas, tools and mechanisms.

Successful candidates will have a strong technical background, be aware of details that matter, have excellent problem-solving abilities, and be exemplary communicators both at the executive and project team level. You will be a peer leader, have the ability to gain stakeholder buy-in, negotiate and lead virtual teams. Your enterprise cloud experience and operational excellence will influence the team’s decisions, provide insight, and help drive secure and robust solutions.

You will evangelize AWS services and influence customers for adopting them. You should be passionate about delivering a great customer experience by deploying AWS solutions and driving innovation, and also be obsessed with contributing to the day-to-day management of customers’ successful migration to AWS.

Key job responsibilities

Responsibilities

You will establish a deep understanding of your customer’s business vision, culture and processes, and evangelize AWS services and influence customers to adopt the right solution at the right time. Customer Solution Managers (CSM) are responsible for four focus areas:

1/Accelerating AWS Adoption through Delivery and Execution

2/Identify & Align on Strategic Opportunities: CSMs work with the Customer Account team to work backwards from the customer to identify and pursue strategic cloud opportunities. These strategic cloud opportunities can include but are not limited to large-scale migrations, GenAI, data and analytics, digital innovation, high performance computing, product innovation, and business agility.

3/Customer Enablement, you will serve as the customer’s cloud journey coach and be the voice of the customer within AWS, evangelizing customer needs to AWS leadership, product, and engineering teams.

4/Implement governance structures to effectively govern both our partnership with the customer, and the customer’s adoption of AWS.

These interconnected focus areas will enable CSMs to effectively drive cloud adoption, pursue strategic growth opportunities, and empower customer success - all of which are critical to achieving the Automotive & Manufacturing IBU’s objectives. By aligning CSM activities, goals, and opportunities under these focus areas, the Automotive & Manufacturing CSM team can ensure a disciplined, customer-centric approach that maximizes business impact and revenue realization for AWS.

CSMs play a critical role supporting account teams/customers throughout the sales process, and the customer's cloud transformation journey, whilst consistently demonstrating measurable value to the customer regardless of engagement model.

CSMs are able to effectively coordinate cross-functional resources, drive disciplined project delivery, and quantify the tangible business benefits that customers realize through their cloud transformation initiatives. This holistic approach to customer engagement, coupled with the CSM's deep understanding of the Automotive & Manufacturing Industry and AWS capabilities; positions CSMs as trusted advisors who can guide customers through every stage of their cloud journey - from initial strategy and planning to migration, modernization, and ongoing optimization.

This position requires 15% - 30% travel across the calendar year to the customer.

Skills & Attributes

Exceptional ability to lead through influence across diverse stakeholder groups

Critical thinking and self-motivation with proven ability to navigate ambiguity

Data-driven decision maker who uses metrics to measure success and drive improvements

Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with ability to tailor messaging to different audiences

Innovative mindset with passion for solving complex customer challenges

Travel 15-30% as needed, primarily for customer facing events.

We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

The HCLS Industries team at AWS is committed to helping customers enable their transformation journeys. Our primary goal is to meet customers where they are and work backwards from their industry-specific needs to transform their business and industry. Our team speaks the language of our customers, focusing on business outcomes and industry use cases in everything we do — whether building products and solutions, selling, delivering, or partnering.

At AWS, we value critical thinking, self-motivation, and the ability to deal with ambiguity. We celebrate innovation, encourage data-driven decision making, and create an environment where diverse perspectives drive better outcomes.

jobs.description:
The Mashruwala Laboratory at the Stowers Institute for Medical Research invites applications for a Research Technician. The laboratory studies bacterial communities through a developmental biology lens, asking how molecular events within genetically identical bacterial cells generate organized behaviors and spatial patterns across a collective. We are particularly interested in regulated cell death, collective cell-fate decisions, and cell-cell communication as routes to discovering general principles of bacterial community development.
The successful candidate will join a collaborative research team and contribute directly to ongoing projects in bacterial community biology.
The position will involve hands-on experimentation. Responsibilities and scientific ownership will be tailored to the individual and can grow substantially with experience and demonstrated independence.

Role and responsibilities

Research technicians are active scientific contributors to the laboratory. Depending on experience, interests, and project needs, responsibilities can include:
Conducting experiments using bacterial genetics, molecular biology, microscopy, phenotypic assays, and related approaches.
Preparing media and reagents; maintaining bacterial strains, plasmids, and laboratory stocks; and helping sustain reliable experimental workflows.
Collecting, organizing, and analyzing quantitative experimental data while maintaining careful and reproducible research records.
Learning, troubleshooting, and optimizing experimental protocols and, with experience, helping develop new methods.
Contributing to experimental planning, interpretation of results, lab discussions, presentations, and manuscripts as appropriate.
Participating in shared laboratory organization and routine tasks that keep the research environment safe, efficient, and collaborative.

Research, mentoring and professional development environment

We combine bacterial genetics, molecular biology, advanced microscopy, quantitative image analysis, computational approaches, phenotypic analysis, and small-scale laboratory automation. Technicians can gain experience across multiple approaches as their projects and interests develop.
At Stowers, research technicians work in a highly collaborative environment with direct access to Ph.D.-level scientific partners in Technology Centers spanning advanced microscopy, genomics, proteomics, computational biology, and related areas.
The Mashruwala Laboratory receives recurring intramural support from the Stowers Institute, providing flexibility to pursue unexpected findings and ambitious long-term questions. Our research is also supported by the Edward Mallinckrodt, Jr. Foundation.
Mentoring is tailored to each researcher’s background and goals and can include experimental design, quantitative reasoning, data analysis, scientific writing and presentations, project organization, and career development. Technicians who demonstrate readiness can take ownership of project components/ projects.

Who should apply

We welcome applicants from diverse scientific backgrounds who are excited by fundamental biological questions and by research that crosses traditional disciplinary boundaries. Prior experience with Vibrio cholerae or bacterial regulated cell death is not required; we particularly welcome applicants who bring complementary expertise.
A bachelor's degree in microbiology, molecular biology, genetics, biochemistry, cell biology, biophysics, computational biology, or a related field. Candidates with a master's degree are encouraged to apply.
Strong hands-on research experience is welcome.
Experience in at least one relevant area, such as microbial genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, microscopy, quantitative analysis, computation, or genomics. Experience in every area is not expected.
Careful organization, attention to detail, reliable record-keeping, and strong follow-through.
Scientific curiosity, persistence, and a willingness to learn new approaches and troubleshoot difficult problems.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

Mashruwala AA, Qin B, Bassler BL. Quorum-sensing- and type VI secretion-mediated spatiotemporal cell death drives genetic diversity in Vibrio cholerae. Cell (2022).
Mashruwala AA, Bassler BL. Quorum sensing orchestrates parallel cell death pathways in Vibrio cholerae via Type 6 secretion-dependent and -independent mechanisms. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (2024).

new_jobs.title: Research Technician - Bacterial Community Development & Regulated Cell Death
new_jobs.description:
The Mashruwala Laboratory at the Stowers Institute for Medical Research invites applications for a Research Technician. The laboratory studies bacterial communities through a developmental biology lens, asking how molecular events within genetically identical bacterial cells generate organized behaviors and spatial patterns across a collective. We are particularly interested in regulated cell death, collective cell-fate decisions, and cell-cell communication as routes to discovering general principles of bacterial community development.
The successful candidate will join a collaborative research team and contribute directly to ongoing projects in bacterial community biology.
The position will involve hands-on experimentation. Responsibilities and scientific ownership will be tailored to the individual and can grow substantially with experience and demonstrated independence.

Role and responsibilities

Research technicians are active scientific contributors to the laboratory. Depending on experience, interests, and project needs, responsibilities can include:
Conducting experiments using bacterial genetics, molecular biology, microscopy, phenotypic assays, and related approaches.
Preparing media and reagents; maintaining bacterial strains, plasmids, and laboratory stocks; and helping sustain reliable experimental workflows.
Collecting, organizing, and analyzing quantitative experimental data while maintaining careful and reproducible research records.
Learning, troubleshooting, and optimizing experimental protocols and, with experience, helping develop new methods.
Contributing to experimental planning, interpretation of results, lab discussions, presentations, and manuscripts as appropriate.
Participating in shared laboratory organization and routine tasks that keep the research environment safe, efficient, and collaborative.

Research, mentoring and professional development environment

We combine bacterial genetics, molecular biology, advanced microscopy, quantitative image analysis, computational approaches, phenotypic analysis, and small-scale laboratory automation. Technicians can gain experience across multiple approaches as their projects and interests develop.
At Stowers, research technicians work in a highly collaborative environment with direct access to Ph.D.-level scientific partners in Technology Centers spanning advanced microscopy, genomics, proteomics, computational biology, and related areas.
The Mashruwala Laboratory receives recurring intramural support from the Stowers Institute, providing flexibility to pursue unexpected findings and ambitious long-term questions. Our research is also supported by the Edward Mallinckrodt, Jr. Foundation.
Mentoring is tailored to each researcher’s background and goals and can include experimental design, quantitative reasoning, data analysis, scientific writing and presentations, project organization, and career development. Technicians who demonstrate readiness can take ownership of project components/ projects.

Who should apply

We welcome applicants from diverse scientific backgrounds who are excited by fundamental biological questions and by research that crosses traditional disciplinary boundaries. Prior experience with Vibrio cholerae or bacterial regulated cell death is not required; we particularly welcome applicants who bring complementary expertise.
A bachelor's degree in microbiology, molecular biology, genetics, biochemistry, cell biology, biophysics, computational biology, or a related field. Candidates with a master's degree are encouraged to apply.
Strong hands-on research experience is welcome.
Experience in at least one relevant area, such as microbial genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, microscopy, quantitative analysis, computation, or genomics. Experience in every area is not expected.
Careful organization, attention to detail, reliable record-keeping, and strong follow-through.
Scientific curiosity, persistence, and a willingness to learn new approaches and troubleshoot difficult problems.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

Select publications

Mashruwala AA, Qin B, Bassler BL. Quorum-sensing- and type VI secretion-mediated spatiotemporal cell death drives genetic diversity in Vibrio cholerae. Cell (2022).
Mashruwala AA, Bassler BL. Quorum sensing orchestrates parallel cell death pathways in Vibrio cholerae via Type 6 secretion-dependent and -independent mechanisms. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (2024).
